punchline: Saying grace is already a Stoic exercise: for a moment, the food might not have been there.
thirty_sec: People get what they want and stop noticing it, William Irvine says, and then they want more. The Stoic fix is to picture the loss briefly and periodically. Epictetus suggested reminding yourself, when parting from a friend, that it might be the last time. Saying grace is a version too. A few times a day or week, not constantly.
